## Intro

This edition covers the week of 23-29 November 2026 and reports developments for commercial road freight in Poland and France, with priority for heavy, oversize and special transport. Reports: Poland extends driving time to 11 hours for domestic LPG tanker drivers until 6 December; Grand Est: blue roadside units prepare a per-kilometre HGV eco-contribution for vehicles over 3.5 t from April 2027.

This edition was prepared after its scheduled release on 2026-11-20T11:00:00.000Z. It covers 2026-W48; the publication date above records the delayed release.

## Lead reports

### Poland extends driving time to 11 hours for domestic LPG tanker drivers until 6 December

According to an e-truckbus.pl industry report, Poland's infrastructure minister has introduced a temporary derogation from the EU rules on driving time, breaks and rest for drivers carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Drivers may drive up to 11 hours per day under the derogation. The report says the derogation applies from 6 November to 6 December 2026.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Poland, domestic LPG transport only. The report does not extend the derogation to international journeys.  
**Affected vehicles:** Tank vehicles carrying LPG (ADR cargo) on domestic Polish journeys, driven by tachograph-using drivers.  
**When:** 6 November 2026 to 6 December 2026

**Impact:** Domestic LPG carriers get more flexible driving-time planning during the derogation period. The report also notes that more flexibility for carriers does not automatically benefit drivers. Cross-border LPG legs are not covered, so the standard EU driving-time and rest rules still apply to them. Tachograph analysis and infringement checks need to reflect the derogation only on qualifying domestic journeys.

**Recommended action:** Read the official Polish ministerial regulation to confirm the exact conditions, the qualifying journeys and any documentation required. Keep domestic LPG legs separate from international legs in dispatch and tachograph analysis. Plan driver rest sensibly and do not assume the derogation applies abroad.

**Exemptions/conditions:** The derogation covers domestic LPG transport only. Applicability to other cargo, to international journeys or to abnormal loads is not confirmed in the report.

*Source: [e-truckbus.pl](https://e-truckbus.pl/czas-jazdy-kierowcow-cystern-lpg-11-godzin/) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*

### Grand Est: blue roadside units prepare a per-kilometre HGV eco-contribution for vehicles over 3.5 t from April 2027 (France)

According to an Autonews report from 18 November 2026, blue roadside units are appearing along roads in the Grand Est region. They prepare a distance-based HGV levy called the éco-contribution poids lourds (ECPL), decided by the Grand Est Region. The report cites a rate of 15 centimes per kilometre and says it targets heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t from April 2027.

**Category:** Infrastructure restriction  
**Where:** Grand Est region, France. The supplied report does not list the specific roads, so no nationwide scope should be assumed.  
**Affected vehicles:** Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t, as stated in the report.  
**When:** Planned from April 2027; the report gives no exact start date.

**Impact:** Carriers running through Grand Est face a new per-kilometre cost from April 2027. The cost matters for quotes, tenders and contract clauses covering routes in the region. The report says the revenue is meant to fund road maintenance and modernisation.

**Recommended action:** Check the official Grand Est Region or national documentation for the exact network, rate, start date, vehicle-class definitions and any exemptions. Review long-term contracts and toll pass-through clauses for Grand Est routes. Model route-cost scenarios, including alternatives that avoid the region, before the April 2027 start.

**Exemptions/conditions:** None confirmed in the supplied report.

*Source: [Autonews](https://www.autonews.fr/actualite/nouvelle-taxe-routiere-avec-larrivee-des-boitiers-bleus-voici-les-vehicules-qui-devront-payer-150755) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*

## Operator checklist

- Poland: Read the official Polish ministerial regulation to confirm the exact conditions, the qualifying journeys and any documentation required. Keep domestic LPG legs separate from international legs in dispatch and tachograph analysis. Plan driver rest sensibly and do not assume the derogation applies abroad.
- France: Check the official Grand Est Region or national documentation for the exact network, rate, start date, vehicle-class definitions and any exemptions. Review long-term contracts and toll pass-through clauses for Grand Est routes. Model route-cost scenarios, including alternatives that avoid the region, before the April 2027 start.
